concerns.text: Phase 5 states that paired t‑tests will compare Model A vs. Model B on the *full* test set, *including proxy rows* (i.e., observations where `is_proxy=True`). Model B is trained only on rows with measured residual stress, so its predictions on proxy rows rely on extrapolation or imputed values. Using these mixed‑type predictions in a paired t‑test violates the assumption that both models are evaluated on the same distribution of inputs and may bias the significance test. The evaluation should either (a) restrict the paired comparison to the subset with measured stress, or (b) ensure Model B can legitimately predict proxy rows (e.g., by training on both measured and proxy data with a flag) before inclusion in the paired test.
